summary: Destroys a linked list rooted at the object's list-header pointer (this+0xC). The header holds head (0x0), tail (0x4), cursor (0x8) and count (0xC). The walk frees every node with FreeWrapper_7bcf; each node whose alive-flag byte at +8 is non-zero (and whose content pointer at +0 is non-null) has its vtable destructor invoked with argument 1 first. After a defensive second traversal, the header itself is freed, its four fields are zeroed, and this+0xC is set to NULL. Called by Sound_Post (004C8CA0).

local_names.a1: object whose +0xC holds the list-header pointer
local_names.v2: next node pointer while walking the chain via +4
local_names.v3: node being freed in the first traversal
local_names.v6: re-read list header before the defensive second traversal
local_names.v7: next node pointer in the second traversal
local_names.v8: node being freed in the second traversal
local_names.v4: zero-test of the node alive-flag byte at +8

operations.description: Read the list header v1 = *(this+0xC); if it is NULL the function does nothing.
If the header's head pointer *v1 is non-null, enter the first traversal over the node chain.

First traversal: for each node read its next pointer at +4 and alive-flag byte at +8; when the flag is non-zero (guard v4 false) and the content pointer at +0 is non-null, invoke the content vtable destructor with argument 1; then free the node with FreeWrapper_7bcf and continue while the next pointer is non-null.
Clear the list-header fields: head, tail, cursor and count at header offsets 0x0, 0x4, 0x8 and 0xC are all zeroed.

Defensive second traversal over the re-read header: for each remaining node call the content vtable destructor with argument 1 when the +8 alive flag is non-zero and the +0 content pointer is non-null, free the node with FreeWrapper_7bcf, then zero the header fields again and free the header itself.
Set this+0xC to 0 so the object no longer references the freed header, and return the header-free result.
Return the result of FreeWrapper_7bcf on the freed list header (the second traversal path), which is garbage-initialized on paths that do not reach that call.
Invoked by Sound_Post (004C8CA0) to tear down the object's node list.

unresolved: The first traversal already frees every node, making the second traversal and header-free appear redundant; this is treated as defensive/residual logic rather than a two-tier list model because no structural difference between the passes is evident
The vtable destructor call signature (content object + integer argument 1) and the meaning of the +8 alive flag are inferred from the field layout only; no class contract is documented
The return value on the header-NULL early path is an uninitialized register, visible in the decompiler as a garbage read
